input.content: Anti-pattern: "simplifying" a cleanup/teardown by removing a conditional identity guard before a destructive map eviction. In cleanup_setup(store, workspace_id, setup_id), the original code only popped store.active[workspace_id] when the currently-active association's setup_id matched the one being cleaned up (`if association and association["setup_id"] == setup_id`). Replacing this with an unconditional `store.active.pop(workspace_id, None)` is a correctness regression: when a newer setup has superseded the old one for the same workspace, a delayed/stale cleanup of the OLD setup_id will now evict the NEWER active association. Rule: a guard that compares an owner/identity field (setup_id, version, owner token) before a destructive delete on shared state is load-bearing — removing it as "dead code" during simplification silently changes behavior under supersession/concurrency. Flag any diff that deletes an identity-match check preceding pop/del/remove on shared maps.
